title: I Took the Notary Window Appointment to the Clerk Who Waved a Cousin

parts.text: I took ticket 19 at 10:33 a.m. and clerk Dina waved a cousin into my numbered window. The screen said: TAKE A TICKET. ONE WINDOW. NO FAMILY CUTS. I was thirty-nine, filer, holding a stamp appointment. Dina shrugged. "Clerks are the window." I photographed the screen, the ticket, and the cousin at my counter. Then I asked for the stamp log. At 10:38 the supervisor pinged why Dina's name was on a waved cut. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The supervisor can see Dina's cousin at window 19 during my appointment.

social.video_title: The clerk waved a cousin into my notary window — Part 1/2
social.description: Notary queue, ticket 19, a family cut. I logged the wave. Would you have asked for the stamp log?

parts.text: Dina called it a quick stamp until the supervisor asked for the still. I printed the log, the ticket, and the photo. The cousin took a ticket. Dina ran the window in order and told the next clerk stamps were always about optics. Optics is a word clerks use when a screen exists. Appointment now has a second line: COUSINS TAKE TICKETS. I keep 19. Dina brown-bags her jokes. The window finally looks like a queue, not a reunion. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Stamp log, a real ticket, and a second line. Was a quick stamp ever my number?
